Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment
Heard Ms.Nithya learned counsel who represents Sri.Prakash.M.H. learned counsel on record for the appellants.

Also heard Sri.B.Pradeep learned counsel for respondent No.1.
2.
The claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
Challenge in the appeal is the order that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, in MVC No.6127/2018, dated 11.02.2020.
The wife and the son of the deceased Thimmaiah (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased' for brevity) filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- in total.
The Tribunal through the impugned order came to a conclusion that the compensation which the appellants are entitled to is Rs.8,44,444/-.

Holding that the deceased contributed to the accident to occur and that contribution is to an extent of 10%, directed the respondents to pay 90% of the awarded compensation i.e.,
Rs.7,60,000/-.

sentences.text: Making her submission Ms.Nithya contends that the amount awarded as compensation is on lower side.
Learned counsel states that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

However,
the Tribunal took the notional income as Rs.8,000/- per month which is erroneous.

Learned counsel states that the accident occurred in the year 2018 and for the relevant period, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking notional income as Rs.12,500/- for assessing compensation and atleast the said figure ought to have been considered by the Tribunal.
Learned counsel Sri.Pradeep.B on the other hand contends that no substantive proof is produced with regard to actual occupation and earnings of the deceased by the date of accident.

However, the learned counsel did not raise any serious objection for taking the notional income as Rs.12,500/-.
6.
It is not in dispute that the deceased died at the age of 55 years.

Therefore, 10% of the actual earnings are required to be added towards future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Also as the dependants of two in members, 1/3rd of the earnings of the deceased are required to be deducted towards personal and living expenses which the deceased would have incurred for himself had he been alive.
Also the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '11' as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma's case.

Therefore, applying aforementioned parameters, loss of dependency if calculated is as under:
NC: 2024:KHC:32775 Amount Description In Rs.
Notional Income per month 12,500-00 Annual Income (12,500X12) 1,50,000-00 Add 10% towards future prospects 1,65,000-00 (1,50,000+10%)

Deduct 1/3rd towards personal and 1,10,000-00 living expenses Loss of dependency on applying 12,10,000-00 appropriate multiplier '11'
7.
Thus the compensation which the appellants are entitled to under the head loss of dependency is Rs.12,10,000/-.
Together with the said amount, the appellants are entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Also the first appellant being the wife of the deceased is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium.
Likewise the second appellant being the son of the deceased is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium.

Thus, the compensation which the appellants are entitled to is as under:
Amount Sl No. Compensation in Rs.
1 Loss of dependency 12,10,000-00 2 Loss of estate 15,000-00 NC: 2024:KHC:32775 3 Funeral expenses 15,000-00 4 Loss of spousal Consortium 40,000-00 5 Loss of parental Consortium 40,000-00
Out of the compensation which the appellants are entitled to i.e., Rs.13,20,000/-, the respondents are liable to pay 90% which comes to Rs.11,88,000/-.
Thus the appeal is required to be allowed in part.

Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following:

3 ORDER

sentences.text: (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation which the appellants are entitled to from the respondents is enhanced from Rs.7,60,000/- to Rs.11,88,000/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
NC: 2024:KHC:32775 (v) On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw their respective shares.
(vi) The apportionment made remains undisturbed.

Sd/-
